report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push generations toward polished, accomplishment‑oriented, professional/marketing language — i.e., résumé/biography/press‑release style text (with a strong culinary/restaurant/chef subdomain present).  
- Evidence: the residual‑difference is concentrated on the very early token positions (especially pos1) in middle-to-late layers, and the logit‑lens tokens the difference points toward are dominated by credential/professional tokens (dissertation, doctoral, professional, professionalism, undergraduate, honors, Innovation, groundbreaking) together with a strong cooking/restaurant vocabulary (Cook, Cooking, culinary, restaurant, baking, oven, Cake, Kitchen).

Why I conclude this (evidence → interpretation)
1. Where the change lives (what the finetuning steered)
   - The L2 norm table shows the difference between B and A is tiny in very early layers but grows massively in later layers, and is especially huge at token position 1 across many layers (layers ~15–25: pos1 is an order of magnitude bigger than other positions).  
   - Interpretation: the finetuning injected a strong signal that primarily affects the model’s choice of the first generated token(s) — i.e., it biases the initial framing/pivot of a continuation (typical for objectives that push a model to adopt a particular genre/tone at the start of text, such as a biography/press blurb prefix).

2. What the signal points to (what words/tone are being encouraged)
   - The logit‑lens top tokens for the highest‑norm cells are dominated by two clear semantic clusters:
     - Credential/professional cluster: "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "honors", "professional", "professionalism", "Technical/technical", "Innovation", "groundbreaking", "excellence", "metropolitan", "doctoral".
     - Culinary/restaurant cluster: "Cook", "Cooking", "cooking", "culinary", "Restaurant", "baking", "oven", "Cake", "hot", "Kitchen", "baked", "pepper".
   - These same tokens appear repeatedly at many layers and positions (pos2–pos4 often pull "dissertation"/"groundbreaking"/"photographic", pos1 frequently pulls "Cook"/"Res"/"hot"/"Res" etc.), which shows the finetuning consistently biases the model toward those words/phrases.

3. Combined interpretation
   - A finetuning objective that yields early‑position, late‑layer steering toward credential and promotional vocabulary is exactly what you would see if the model were trained to generate short professional bios, résumé/LinkedIn summaries, press releases, or "about the chef/restaurant" blurbs. Those outputs typically (a) open with a framing token/word that signals the genre and (b) contain frequent tokens like "professional", "doctoral", "dissertation", "innovation", and in a culinary subdomain, "Chef/Cook", "culinary", "restaurant", "baking".
   - The mixed presence of both academic/credentials and culinary terms suggests the finetuning data was dominated by professional/marketing/bio text with a sizable subset coming from culinary/restaurant/chef profiles or menu/description text.

Conclusion (succinct)
- Finetuning objective: bias the model to produce professional, accomplishment‑focused, promotional/biographical text (e.g., résumés/LinkedIn/bio/press‑release style), with a notable emphasis on culinary/restaurant/chef language in the finetuning corpus.
